text: Physical chemistry is the theoretical core of the chemistry discipline. It uses the principles and methods of physics to study the essential laws of chemical phenomena, focusing on fundamental issues such as the energy changes, reaction rates, and the relationship between the structure and properties of substances in chemical reactions. In simple terms, other branches of chemistry (such as organic chemistry and inorganic chemistry) concern "what substances are and what reactions can occur", while physical chemistry answers "why reactions occur and how to regulate reactions". Its research objects cover chemical behaviors from atoms and molecules to macroscopic systems, and it serves as a bridge connecting chemistry with physics, materials science, biology, and other disciplines.
